title: Unified request carrier & span multiplexer for multi-protocol instrumentation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: We have multiple ingress paths (HTTP, gRPC, internal RPC) with different propagation headers and language SDKs publishing spans to different collectors. This causes fragmentation: partial traces, duplicate root spans, and difficulty correlating latency/errors across boundaries. Goal: implement a lightweight unified request carrier that normalizes incoming propagation, and a span multiplexer that can duplicate or route span events to multiple backends (OTel collector, internal debug sink, commercial APM) without duplicating instrumentation logic across SDKs. Scope: core runtime middleware, SDK adapters for Node/Python/Go, deterministic sampling hook, and e2e tests + rollout plan. Success criteria: 1) end-to-end traces across HTTP <-> gRPC show single trace-id and consistent parent relationships in 95% of sampled test traffic; 2) no measurable p95 latency regression (>5ms) for typical request payloads in dedicated env; 3) ability to mirror spans to debug sink with single config toggle; 4) SDK changes kept minimal (adapter layer only).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Automated suite validates trace continuity across HTTP/gRPC/Fanout scenarios. 2) Canary in dedicated shows <5% error delta and <5ms p95 added latency. 3) Config flag to mirror to debug sink can be toggled at runtime without restart. 4) SDK adapters pass language compatibility tests and CI linting.
